A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same vHeat/HCO research. All 18 pages of v1 and 16 pages of v2, including equations, figures, tables and appendices, support comparison despite extensive reformatting and reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original ImageNet-1K, COCO and ADE20K experiments, computational measurements, ablations and visualizations.

after.justification: V2 retains original experiments and adds out-of-distribution classification, image restoration, implementation comparisons and gate ablations.

M1.justification: The HCO equations, frequency embeddings and gating mechanism remain unchanged. V2 adds vHeatIR by replacing SwinIR attention with HCO and revises the stated backbone depths and widths, including a narrower, deeper vHeat-B outside semantic segmentation (v1 Table 4; v2 Table 8). These adapt the retained method.

E1.justification: Beyond retained ImageNet-1K, COCO and ADE20K coverage, v2 evaluates ObjectNet and ImageNet-A for distribution shift, Set12 and McMaster for grayscale/color denoising, and LIVE1 for JPEG artifact reduction (Tables 4–5). This substantially broadens the evaluated tasks and input conditions.

E2.justification: The full ImageNet comparison adds DCFormer-SW, RepLKNet-31B and Vim-B while dropping DeiT, HiViT and XCiT rows. ADE20K adds ViL-S/B and removes ResNet, DeiT+MLN and Vim-S rows. New restoration comparisons use DnCNN, DRUNet and SwinIR; Appendix J adds MetaFormer-v2-M48, CAFormer-B36, iFormer-B and BiFormer-B.

E3.justification: V2 revises task-specific backbone configurations and changes ADE20K FLOPs measurement from 512×2048 to 512×512, while retaining the 512×512 training input. It adds downstream FPS measurements and restoration evaluation using PSNR, denoising noise level 15 and JPEG quality 40, plus a visualization after 15,000 training iterations.

E4.justification: V2 adds distribution-shift robustness tests, Linear+SiLU replacement/removal and HCO-removal ablations, a matrix-DCT versus Torch-DCT efficiency comparison, and a denoising case study. It removes the before-training ERF comparison and HiViT panels. The GFNet and layerwise thermal-diffusivity analyses are retained through relocation.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run counts, error bars, confidence intervals or significance tests. V2 continues reporting point estimates without adding uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: V2 adds OOD results, including 26.7% ObjectNet and 36.8% ImageNet-A accuracy for vHeat-B, alongside restoration, FPS and gate-ablation results. Existing entries also change: vHeat-B ImageNet accuracy/parameters/FLOPs change from 83.9%/87M/14.9G to 84.0%/68M/11.2G; COCO 1× vHeat-T mask AP changes from 41.0 to 41.2; ADE20K vHeat-S mIoU changes from 49.0 to 49.1. Revised configurations and profiling settings limit direct performance comparisons.

T1.justification: The heat-equation derivation, Neumann boundary assumption, DCT/IDCT construction and complexity argument are retained. V2 omits v1's explicit inverse-Fourier integral expansion but preserves the equivalent solution, without substantive changes to mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: V2 explicitly presents HCO as plug-and-play and extends its superiority claims to OOD classification and low-level vision. It replaces the advertised savings of over 70% memory and over 30% FLOPs with 80% and 35%. The central heat-conduction, global-receptive-field and efficiency contributions remain.

C2.justification: V2 removes v1's limitations concerning difficult long-range dependency learning and the absence of a self-supervised learning method. It adds interpretations connecting restoration performance to frequency-domain processing and attributing gains primarily to HCO rather than gating. Most existing mechanism explanations remain or move between sections.

D1.justification: V2 states that code is available, adds that parameters/FLOPs are reported after HCO reparameterization, and revises Tiny training time from 5 to 4.5 minutes per epoch. It omits v1's special no-DWConv recipe: batch size 1024, learning rate 0.001 and weight decay 0.05. This omission does not establish that the underlying recipe changed.

R1.justification: V2 adds citations for OOD benchmarks, restoration methods and datasets, Vision-LSTM, DCFormer and additional backbones, plus LLaMA attribution for the gated branch. Section 2's positioning among CNNs, ViTs, state-space models and physics-inspired work, including QB-Heat, remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 rewrites the abstract and substantially reorganizes the experimental narrative into results, dynamic-locality analysis and global-filter comparisons. It moves GFNet and frequency-prior discussion into the main text, moves ERF analysis into the appendix, and restructures the supplementary sections. Title, authorship and acknowledgement text also change.

P2.justification: The main text switches from one to two columns. The efficiency plots are redrawn and moved to the opening page; the combined detection/segmentation table is split, with FPS replacing parameter columns. V2 adds restoration, robustness and gate-ablation displays and a backbone comparison plot, while simplifying the ERF figure.

improvement.justification: V2 strengthens empirical support through distribution-shift and restoration experiments, additional component controls and downstream speed measurements. The net gain is limited by removal of v1's substantive limitations and special no-DWConv training recipe. Changed backbone and profiling settings also restrict conclusions drawn from the updated accuracy and efficiency numbers.
